items.title: In Goa, real estate land grab threatens protected eco-sensitive slopes
items.summary: Right before the Mapusa river meets the Mandovi river near Panjim, it crosses the wetlands, creeks and low lying paddy fields of Salvador Do Mundo. Surrounding these large stretches of paddy fields are houses and forested hills with steep slopes. Telangana-based real-estate company, KGL Realtors Private Limited bought 20,000 square metres of land on one of these hills. When the land was bought, the sale deed described it as “barren and waste land”. In Goa, a state-wide regional plan dictates what activities are permitted on a piece of land. The land that KGL bought is zoned as eco-sensitive land where development is regulated. It specifically categorises all of it as Natural Cover and part (4,000 square metres) of it as Natural Cover with “No Development Slopes”. The Regional Plan 2021 , published in 2010, marked nearly 82% of the state as eco-sensitive zones, providing them with protection from rampant construction and development. Land is a state subject in India and all states have town planning acts which govern spatial planning. But other than seven states, these acts only focus on urban areas. In Goa, the regional plan was created based on the provisions of the Town and Country Planning Act (TCP Act) and covers the entire state. Over the last eight years, the government has introduced three successive amendments to the Act allowing the government to do plot-by-plot change of zones in the regional plan. The latest of these amendments was introduced in 2024 as Section 39A, which allows land owners to apply for zone changes of their plots. items.title: Dharmasthala case explained: The latest findings and unanswered questions
items.summary: A lot has happened since we last spoke about the Dharmasthala case. And because we’ve been following this story closely and reporting on it through all these developments, I thought it was time we sat down and made sense of where things stand. Last year, the focus was on Chinnaiah - the masked man who came forward with massive claims about mass burials in and around Dharmasthala. But that story eventually fell apart. The state government constituted a Special Investigation Team, or SIT, to investigate his allegations. But instead of the hundreds of bodies that Chinnaiah had initially claimed he had buried, the excavations unearthed just two skeletons- both male. Chinnaiah subsequently changed his version. He was arrested, and the SIT initiated perjury proceedings against him. He has also alleged that he was forced by a few people to make these claims and they were also booked by the police. But now, there are new developments. The Karnataka State Women’s Commission has written to the state government asking for the SIT’s mandate to be expanded. Why? Because the SIT in its status report to the Commission points at discrepancies in records relating to Unnatural Death Reports, or UDRs. The SIT also found remains of 7 people at a location called Banglegudde. Then there has been another major development: the Supreme Court has ordered a fresh investigation into the 2012 rape and murder of 17-year-old Sowjanya. So, what exactly are all these developments? These included the part refinancing of existing project loans through ₹8,000 crore in rupee term loans from a consortium comprising the National Bank for Financing Infrastructure and Development, India Infrastructure Finance Company Limited, ICICI Bank Limited, UCO Bank and Punjab & Sind Bank; a ₹2,000 crore working capital demand loan from Bank of Baroda; and fund-based and non-fund-based credit facilities aggregating to ₹400 crore from ICICI Bank. The refinancing transaction featured a bilateral lending structure supported by a consolidated security package held in trust by a common Security Trustee, requiring consistency across the financing and security documentation. SAM acted as legal counsel to HPCL Rajasthan Refinery across these arrangements, advising on financing and security structuring, applicable regulatory considerations, and the negotiation and finalisation of the relevant finance and security documents. The transaction team consisted of Deepto Roy (Partner), Dnyanraj Desai (Partner), Abhinav Rawat (Principal Associate), Aditya Menon (Associate) and Prashant Dubey (Associate). The term loan proceeds will be utilised for the part refinancing of existing project loans, while the working capital facilities will support HRRL’s working capital requirements and help address cash flow mismatches associated with the project, including its allied utilities and facilities at Pachpadra, District Balotra, Rajasthan. The project, with a refining capacity of 9 MMTPA and integrated petrochemical production capacity of 2.4 MMTPA, is expected to strengthen India’s refining and petrochemical value chain, enhance supply security and support industrial development. items.title: Lula is declared winner of Brazil's election as Bolsonaro rejects results
items.summary: By Eléonore Hughes, Mauricio Savarese And Anna-catherine Brigida Brazil’s President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, a vocal critic of U.S. President Donald Trump, was reelected Sunday in a result that provides relief to critics of widening U.S. influence in Latin America . With 100% of the vote counted, Brazil’s electoral court announced that the soon to be 81-year-old Lula had a lead of nearly 4.4 million votes over opponent Flávio Bolsonaro, giving him 51.8% of the total vote. Bolsonaro quickly refused to concede defeat and asked for the election results to be annulled after an evening of chaos at some polling places that followed a last-minute decision to extend voting by two hours. Bolsonaro is the son of former President Jair Bolsonaro, whom Lula defeated to take the presidency in 2022. Lula's triumph bucks a regional trend of victories for right-of-center presidential candidates allied with Trump. It also means Latin America’s largest economy, with a GDP of $2.6 trillion per year, will likely continue defying Trump’s demands, despite the pressure of increased tariffs . Lula says Brazil is ‘not anyone’s backyard' A video published by Lula’s campaign shows the veteran leader celebrating with First Lady Rosângela da Silva and allies after his runoff victory was confirmed by Brazil’s electoral court. Wearing star-shaped red glasses, he kissed his wife. Speaking to his supporters, thousands of whom gathered on Sao Paulo's main artery and in Rio de Janeiro's Cinelandia Square, Lula expressed his gratitude to the Brazilian people, and pledged to respect all Brazilians, regardless of gender or religion. He also attacked Bolsonaro. “This was a defeat for denialism and lies. I must confess that every time I attended a debate, I felt embarrassed,” he said. He also doubled down on his commitment to Brazil’s sovereignty. “Either the homeland remains free, or we die for Brazil,” he said. “This country will not accept being anyone’s backyard.” In Rio de Janeiro, cars beeped their horns and a woman dressed in red — the color of Lula supporters — shouted “You lost! items.title: Hyderabad: BJP MP Eatala Rajender to lead march over Jawahar Nagar dumpyard pollution
items.summary: BJP MP from Telangana Eatala Rajender has called for an end to fresh garbage being brought to Hyderabad’s Jawahar Nagar dumpyard, and for the waste already accumulated there to be processed and recycled. The Malkajgiri MP said that the pollution from the site is causing serious health problems for people in nearby neighbourhoods including Yapral, Dammaiguda, Kapra, Alwal, among others. As part of a campaign against the dumpyard, the BJP leader has announced a march beginning October 27. Speaking at a roundtable meeting he organised on Sunday, October 25, Eatala Rajender called for waste-processing facilities with zero-pollution technology. He said waste could be converted into electricity, biogas and organic manure rather than dumped indiscriminately. He also said he would seek support and funding from the Union government in this regard. The MP said that pollution from the Jawahar Nagar dumpyard affects areas within a 25-to-30-kilometre radius and that residents face hazardous living conditions. He questioned why, despite court orders and the resources of the private waste-management company Ramky Enviro Engineers operating at the site, residents’ concerns remained unresolved. He also alleged that the company’s corporate social responsibility funds were being spent outside the state instead of on local drinking water, roads and other facilities. items.title: Youth protests across Europe: the overlapping crises facing Gen Z
items.summary: Young people are facing a future that feels increasingly uncertain. Although every generation experiences turbulence while navigating adolescence, the pressures experienced by Gen Z – those born between 1997 and 2012 – are different and seem more pervasive. From climate change and mental health concerns to academic pressure, housing costs, job and economic insecurity, today’s young people are navigating a complex set of expectations. Understanding their frustrations, including those expressed through protests across Europe, requires looking beyond individual experiences to the social conditions shaping their lives. Adolescence has long been seen as a period of “storm and stress”. This reflecting a belief that is a universal and inevitable period of emotional turmoil, behavioural conflict and identity crisis. However, this has been increasingly challenged. Rather than being defined solely by difficulty and disruption, adolescence is increasingly viewed as a period of possibility, opportunity and growth . Yet realising that potential depends heavily on the social environments in which young people grow up. A growing body of evidence highlights adolescence as a critical developmental period with profound implications for future health and wellbeing. There is also increasing recognition that adolescence extends well beyond the teenage years and well into the twenties . Growing up under pressure Young people nowadays grow up under intense and often overlapping pressure, and today this is to a higher extent than generations before. Evidence from the World Health Organization’s Health Behaviour in School-aged Children study suggests that school-related pressure increased between 2002 and 2022 across many countries. In 2022 , among 15-year-old girls, almost two-thirds reported feeling pressured by schoolwork, compared with less than half of boys. The same research documented declines in perceived family and peer support. In other words, young people appear to be facing increasing demands while some of the social resources that help them cope with those demands are weakening. Young people are feeling educational pressure. Parental expectations and criticism have also intensified in many contexts. items.title: Lula re-elected in Brazil, Bolsonaro rejects verdict
items.summary: By ELÉONORE HUGHES, MAURICIO SAVARESE and ANNA-CATHERINE BRIGIDA Associated Press Brazil's President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, a vocal critic of U.S. President Donald Trump, was reelected Sunday in a result that provides relief to critics of widening U.S. influence in Latin America. With 100% of the vote counted, Brazil's electoral court announced that the soon to be 81-year-old Lula had a lead of nearly 4.4 million votes over opponent Flávio Bolsonaro, giving him 51.8% of the total vote. Bolsonaro quickly refused to concede defeat and asked for the election results to be annulled after an evening of chaos at some polling places that followed a last-minute decision to extend voting by two hours. Lula's triumph bucks a regional trend of victories for right-of-center presidential candidates allied with Trump. It also means Latin America's largest economy, with a GDP of $2.6 trillion per year, will likely continue defying Trump's demands, despite the pressure of increased tariffs. Lula's win confirmed by electoral court A video published by Lula's campaign shows the veteran leader celebrating with First Lady Rosângela da Silva and allies after his runoff victory was confirmed by Brazil's electoral court. Wearing star-shaped red glasses, he kissed his wife. Hundreds of his supporters began gathering on Sao Paulo's main artery to celebrate the victory. In Rio de Janeiro, cars beeped their horns and a woman dressed in red — the color of Lula supporters — shouted "You lost! Cry harder!" to four men in yellow and green sipping beers, Bolsonaro's signature colors. A huge roar echoed in the street as the result was confirmed. Rodrigo Valentim, a 51-year-old businessman and supporter of Bolsonaro, said that another Lula government would harm the economy. He pointed to financial markets' positive reaction to the result of the first round, when Bolsonaro bested Lula. "I don't understand how people can vote for Lula," he said. "The country is collapsing." Lula is set to begin his fourth non-consecutive term as president on Jan. 5, 2027. items.title: Tamil finfluencer Harish’s death exposes enforcement gap in regulating financial advisers
items.summary: The death of a 27-year-old Tamil financial influencer V Harish has triggered a polarising discussion on social media. The Chennai police have arrested YouTuber Jason Samuel on suicide abetment charges, and the case is currently under investigation. The tragic death has put a spotlight on India’s largely unregulated finfluencer (short for financial influencer) landscape. Harish, who ran the “Finance with Harish” account, had more than 1.3 million followers. He died by suicide on October 20, days after YouTuber Jason Samuel published a video questioning his credentials, alleging that he had offered securities-related advice without the required Stock and Exchanges Board of India (SEBI) registration. Harish’s Instagram account had also been suspended. Samuel alleged that Meta, the parent company of Instagram, acted after receiving reports about Harish’s alleged misleading content but the circumstances of the suspension have not been independently established. Harish’s family accused Jason, arrested on charges of abetting suicide, of harassment and extortion. The case has stirred a debate over whether online criticism crossed into cyberbullying. Jason has denied these allegations. Besides the argument of cyberbullying and accountability, the case also points to a failure of the government to monitor financial content online. What SEBI’s rules on financial advice say SEBI’s Investment Advisers Regulations explicitly require registration before a person acts or holds themselves out as an investment adviser. The rules generally cover the business of providing investment advice for consideration. They exempt good-faith general comments on market trends when those comments do not identify a particular security or investment product. The regulations state that “no person shall act as an investment adviser or hold itself out as an investment adviser unless he has obtained a certificate of registration from the Board.” While Jason has accused Harish of offering financial advice without the requisite SEBI registration, Harish did not respond to the allegations.
